## LLM Recipe

### 1.3 Pretraining &amp; Optimization

#### [Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26809>)

New comparative experiments test search-native pretraining, which inserts query and retrieval blocks into ordinary text while masking retrieved passages from the prediction loss. Models retain stronger search-based question answering after shared post-training, giving builders evidence for teaching retrieval use earlier alongside clear tradeoffs in closed-book capability and data-preparation cost.

## AI Agent Dev

### 2.8 Agent Evaluation &amp; Security

#### [SkillPrivus: Uncovering PRIVacy of USe Harms in Agentic Skills](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26747>)

SkillPrivus audits installable agent skills before execution by extracting evidence-linked personal-data operations from instructions and code, then assessing their scope and recipients against the advertised purpose and context. Its public-skill study and reviewable privacy cards show how ordinary functionality can raise privacy concerns, while the static, model-dependent flags remain distinct from demonstrated breaches or safety certification.

## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.2 RL &amp; Rollout Infrastructure

#### [CTRL: Concurrent Training and Rollout through GPU Co-Residency](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27119>)

CTRL keeps a host-owned learner and persistent rollout engine concurrently on every GPU, using bounded layer streaming and a policy-publication gate to overlap complete updates with generation under a staleness bound. Matched-learner controls show when sharing a GPU beats time-sharing or whole-device splits, giving reinforcement-learning builders a concrete way to use decoding’s spare compute capacity. The authors report 1.11–2.24× system-throughput gains across 24 workload settings, but substantial host memory and workload balance are prerequisites, and some whole-GPU splits still win.

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

#### [Weave: Routing-Adaptive Warp Scheduling for MoE Megakernels](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27765>)

Weave chooses spatial warp allocations and phase-dependent communication roles from each GPU’s routing counts, keeping matrix units active inside a fused mixture-of-experts layer. Its NVIDIA and AMD layer benchmarks show how runtime scheduling can reduce communication and computation imbalance without changing expert routing. Reported layer speedups are substantially larger than the paper’s broader-path latency controls, so they should not be interpreted as whole-request throughput gains.

### 3.6 Low-Precision &amp; Efficient Execution

#### [IsoMoE: Placement-Invariant Hybrid CPU-GPU Inference with Lossless 12-bit Experts](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27604>)

IsoMoE makes hybrid CPU/GPU expert placement an execution choice by having the GPU replay the CPU’s arithmetic, while a CPU-oriented lossless 12-bit layout reduces expert-memory traffic. An exact dual-microbatch pipeline preserves whole-batch operator shapes and merge order, allowing cached experts to move without changing greedy outputs under a fixed hardware, software and request-batch configuration. On one Xeon 8488C / RTX A6000 server, the authors report 1.26× average decode speedup over the fastest tested baseline across three MoE models; the placement guarantee is not cross-platform or batch invariance.
